_about: Curated, operator-maintained data for offshore-north-dashboard.html (the companion page to the Offshore North podcast). Everything here is dated and sourced; the live pieces (latest campaign posts, latest headlines) come from api/offshore_north_dashboard.json, refreshed by scripts/fetch_offshore_north_dashboard.py. Update this file after a milestone, a result, or a position fix — never invent a fix. Verified 2026-09-19 against the URLs in each entry.

campaign.skipper_line: President and skipper. Came to the sport from engineering and business (26 years leading JMP Solutions). Holds the double-handed course record for the RORC Transatlantic Race; 4th in the 2024 New York Vendée, his first solo IMOCA race. Collingwood, Ontario.
campaign.goal: Become the first Canadian to finish the Vendée Globe — solo, non-stop, unassisted around the world — at the 2028 edition.
campaign.initiative: Be Water Positive (water-scarcity awareness) + a Youth Pathway Programme for young Canadian sailors.
campaign.entry_name: Canada Ocean Racing – Be Water Positive

pedigree.text: Won The Ocean Race as Mālama (11th Hour Racing Team, Charlie Enright)
4th, New York Vendée (Sébastien Simon, as Groupe Dubreuil)
3rd in the Vendée Globe with Sébastien Simon, most of the course on one foil after early-December damage; solo 24-hour record on this hull
Acquired by Canada Ocean Racing, renamed EMIRA IV; 6th in The Ocean Race Europe; retired from the Rolex Fastnet Race

Delivered France → Canada (Atlantic, St Lawrence Seaway, Welland Canal, Great Lakes); first Canadian summer training programme on Georgian Bay, June–August; departed Collingwood 8–9 August; heading back to Europe (team post, 2 September)

position_log.text: Arrived in Collingwood, Ontario, for the summer training programme on Georgian Bay.
Departed Collingwood (weekend of 8–9 August), earlier than the published mid-August plan.
Welland Canal transit posted on the team's YouTube channel.
"Emira IV now leaving Canada and heading back to Europe" — Scott's Notes, Thank you, Canada.

entries.boat: Canada Ocean Racing – Be Water Positive (EMIRA IV)

outline: Complete at least one Grade 2 solo race from the IMOCA 2025–2028 calendar on the boat you will race in the Vendée Globe, finishing within twice the winner's time.
Be among the top 37 in the IMOCA Globe Series championship (remaining places under the organisers' criteria).
The fleet is capped at 40 boats.

lineage.text: Won the very first Route du Rhum in 1978 — 47 years old, in the 12-metre trimaran Olympus Photo, by 98 seconds after 23 days at sea. He died in 2022, aged 90.

Lying second in the 1996–97 Vendée Globe when his last message from the South Pacific described 15-metre seas and 80-knot winds. Never heard from again; wreckage of Groupe LG 2 reached Chile months later.
Campaigned Spirit of Canada through the round-the-world races of the 2000s and started a Vendée Globe; no Vendée finish. Died in 2016.
Chapter four. No Canadian has ever completed the Vendée Globe.

cast.name: Scott Shawyer
cast.boat: Canada Ocean Racing – Be Water Positive (EMIRA IV)
cast.line: The spine of the show: first Canadian bid to finish the Vendée Globe. The Route du Rhum will be his first solo transatlantic on a foiling IMOCA.

cast.name: Sam Goodchild
cast.line: The form skipper going into the Rhum: won the 48H Azimut two years running, set the class Runs record at 32.1 knots in September 2026, second in the 2026 Vendée Arctique.

cast.name: Ambrogio Beccaria
cast.line: The season's breakout: won the 2026 Vendée Arctique in his first solo race on the boat, from fifth in the final windless miles; second in the 48H Azimut.

cast.name: Jérémie Beyou
cast.line: Fourth in the 2024–25 Vendée Globe, third in the 2026 48H Azimut; announced on 10 September 2026 that after ten years with Charal he wants to move up to the Ultim class.

cast.name: Sébastien Simon
cast.line: Third in the 2024–25 Vendée Globe on the hull that is now EMIRA IV, much of it on one foil; now on a new boat launched in August 2026.

cast.name: Paul Meilhat
cast.line: Won the inaugural Ocean Race Atlantic in September 2026 by 8 minutes 56 seconds after eight days at sea.

cast.name: Boris Herrmann
cast.line: Germany's star; led The Ocean Race Atlantic early and finished fourth after a collision with a marine animal damaged the port foil ram.

cast.name: Francesca Clapcich
cast.line: Second in The Ocean Race Atlantic 2026 by under nine minutes; entered in the Rhum.

cast.name: Violette Dorange
cast.line: The youngest finisher of the 2024–25 Vendée Globe and its breakout star; third in the 2026 Vendée Arctique.

cast.name: Kojiro Shiraishi
cast.line: Third in The Ocean Race Atlantic 2026 with Sam Davies aboard.

cast.name: Conrad Colman
cast.line: Finished a Vendée Globe under jury rig; sixth in The Ocean Race Atlantic 2026 with the first all-New Zealand IMOCA crew.

cast.name: Charlie Dalin
cast.line: Won the 2024–25 Vendée Globe in a record 64 days 19 hours while being treated for cancer. He died on 11 June 2026, aged 42; the 2028 race is discussed in his shadow.
